question: Can reviewed clicks proceed while unrelated animation runs, using only browser-owned compositor evidence, while a changed reviewed pixel, a visually identical target swap, navigation, renderer restart and device loss still deliver nothing?
change: Viz copies the reviewed rectangle out of every frame it draws for the reviewed surface and compares the bytes with its own reference copy. A mismatch or failed copy closes the review through the shared gate; an admitted click is released only after Viz verifies a drawn frame at or after the frame active at admission. Renderer-reported damage is not used. Recipient checks stay in the renderer at delivery.
previous: reports/fawn-workspace/20261122-reviewed-input-orderings: any activated frame closed the review; 0 of 20 clicks delivered under unrelated animation.

revisions.sourceIdentity: Each of the 72 touched Chromium files equals pinned Chromium 4a6fb385 plus chromium-doe-runtime.patch plus chromium-reviewed-input.patch, checked file by file against the build overlay.
revisions.build: Linux x86_64 component build (is_debug=false, dcheck_always_on=false). Diagnostic configuration, not the release profile; the non-component release build of the same source was generated and is still compiling.

applicationGuarantees: Kept separate. Drawing and authenticated workspace runs on both arms: lookalike rejected, one fresh write, duplicate commit returned the original receipt, a late version change refused by the application; workspace test passed 20 of 20 per arm on the final build.

workspaceRepeats.earlierBuildsSameViz: 4 first-capture refusals ('visual surface changed or unsupported') in 90 earlier runs before refusal reasons were reported; none in 80 runs since. Fail-closed, nothing delivered. Refusals now name their cause.

profile.note: Profile of the path that ships, not the predeclared backend decision run (backend-predeclaration.json in 20261122-reviewed-input-orderings). Load: compositor, main-thread and canvas animation outside the rectangle plus 4 ms of main-thread work every 16 ms. 300 clicks per arm, one launch each.
findings: Admission itself is ~0.1 ms p99 (validation to compare-and-exchange). The wait is Viz's pixel verdict plus renderer delivery.
Software compositing (cpu) verifies in ~2.3 ms p99; SwiftShader GL compositing (dawn arm) takes ~20 ms p99 because the readback completes a frame later. Click p99: 22.2 ms cpu, 55.4 ms dawn arm.

The doe arm's --gpu-sandbox-start-early keeps SwiftShader GL from initializing, so Viz falls back to software compositing; its numbers match the cpu arm. The same flag on the Dawn runtime causes the same fallback.
No arm obtains a WebGPU adapter on this host (no hardware GPU used), and the reviewed-click path does no WebGPU work. Dawn versus Doe is not measured by this profile.
An open review costs one 9216-byte readback per drawn frame of the reviewed surface; frame pacing stayed at 60 fps with no long frames, and GPU-process RSS rose 4-6 MiB.
GPU-internal blits and driver transfers are not observable here and are recorded as unknown.

decision: Ship the region-scoped Viz verification on the current CPU readback path. Doe is not a requirement for reviewed clicks. A Dawn/Doe decision needs a GPU-resident compare stage and a hardware GPU window (AMD outside the Flash reservation, or Apple M3).
